profile.name: Jaru Iori N. Jardeleza
profile.headline: Learning in public. Building with purpose.
profile.intro: I build and document practical systems across cloud infrastructure, Linux, web, mobile, databases, and local AI — turning coursework into working software. Klightten is the growing library of what I learn, improve, and release.
profile.about:
I’m Jaru Iori N. Jardeleza, a BSIT student at Pateros Technological College and an aspiring cloud engineer. I learn best when an idea has to survive outside a lesson: on real hardware, with real limits, and with enough documentation that I can understand it again later.

Klightten is the identity I give to that process. It brings together my work in Linux, cloud infrastructure, web systems, mobile applications, databases, and local AI. Each project is evidence of what I understood at that point—and a starting place for the next improvement.

works.title: KLIGHTTEN CLOUD
works.summary: An always-online Linux server I set up and run over SSH — the hands-on path I am taking into cloud engineering.
works.description:
An always-online Linux server that I set up and operate over SSH, and the project I am using to learn cloud engineering on real hardware instead of in a sandbox. I wanted the work to involve a machine that actually has to stay reachable, so I started with remote administration: system updates, firewall rules, and service configuration.

The next layer is hosted services, Nginx, DNS, HTTPS, monitoring, and automation. Keeping the stack modest enough for a student budget and limited hardware is the decision that shapes the choices, and documenting each step is the part that makes it useful later.
works.role: Solo build — server setup, remote Linux administration, and documentation.

works.title: KLIGHTTEN Keyboard
works.summary: A released Linux companion for supported SteelSeries Apex keyboards: OLED text and GIF animation, playlists, system monitoring, installable themes, and optional RGB controls.
works.description:
A lightweight Linux companion for supported SteelSeries Apex keyboards, covering OLED text and GIF animation, playlists, system monitoring, installable themes, and optional RGB controls. I built it because I wanted the keyboard on my own desktop to work fully under Linux, and because it is the kind of tool that only exists if someone writes it.

The hard part was device ownership: keeping udev rules and HID access stable so the keyboard stays available to the rest of the system while the app is running. It is released and still maintained, and it is where I learned most about making software work on hardware I do not control.
works.role: Solo developer and maintainer — desktop interface, udev/HID handling, and releases.

works.title: BagHaven Full System
works.summary: A complete online storefront with customer accounts, carts, wishlists, and checkout, plus a protected administrator workspace backed by Supabase and PostgreSQL.
works.description:
A full online storefront — customer accounts, carts, wishlists, checkout, orders, inventory, coupons, and announcements — with a protected workspace where an administrator manages all of it. I built it to understand what a complete system involves past the storefront screens: authentication, roles, and data that has to stay consistent between a customer's cart and the inventory behind it.

The decision that shaped the build was modelling the store in Supabase and PostgreSQL first and letting the React interface follow that schema, instead of fitting the data to the screens. Building the administrator side myself is what made the permission boundaries concrete.
works.role: Solo developer — storefront interface, Supabase data model, and the protected administrator workspace.

works.title: KLIGHTTEN AI
works.summary: A Flutter assistant for Linux and Android, connecting local GGUF models through llama.cpp with room for optional online APIs.
works.description:
A personal assistant for Linux and Android that connects a Flutter interface to local GGUF models through llama.cpp, with room for optional online APIs. I built it because I wanted an assistant that runs on my own machine and stays useful without depending on a paid service.

The decision that mattered was keeping the model layer local and swappable: the interface talks to llama.cpp through a narrow boundary, so an online provider can be added without rewriting the app.
works.role: Solo developer — Flutter interface and local GGUF model integration.

works.title: EqualLearn
works.summary: A responsive learning system for administrators, teachers, and students, developed by a five-student team for gender equality education and awareness at Pateros Technological College.
works.description:
A responsive learning system for administrators, teachers, and students, built by a five-student capstone team at Pateros Technological College for gender equality education and awareness. I contributed as a team member rather than leading it, so it is documented here as collaborative academic work.

The system had to serve three roles at once — administrator, teacher, and student — on hosting and a database that a student team could cover, which shaped how the data and pages were organised. It is deployed and reachable, and working inside a shared codebase taught me how much of the work is coordination.
works.role: Team member in a five-student capstone team at Pateros Technological College.

works.title: KLIGHTTEN Media
works.summary: A Linux desktop media experience for local and online playback, anime workflows, background media, custom themes, playlists, keyboard controls, and a floating player.
works.description:
A Linux desktop media experience for local and online playback, built around keyboard control, anime workflows, custom themes, and a floating player. It grew out of my own desktop setup, where I wanted playback, playlists, and background media to stay inside one interface instead of several.

The technical decision was embedding Qt WebEngine beside mpv: the interface stays web-shaped, while playback goes to a proven media backend.
works.role: Solo developer — player interface, theming, and media integration.

works.title: KLIGHT Panel V3 Custom
works.summary: A custom lightweight bottom panel designed to replace the standard XFCE panel with system dashboards, accessibility controls, session tools, media integration, and a compact Klightten identity.
works.description:
A custom lightweight bottom panel built to replace the standard XFCE panel, with system dashboards, accessibility controls, session tools, and media integration. It exists because I wanted the desktop I use every day to behave the way I need it to, in the Klightten visual language.

The decision behind it was extending GTK 3 and XFCE rather than replacing the desktop environment, which keeps the panel light enough for modest hardware.
works.role: Solo developer — panel interface and XFCE integration.

works.title: Klightten Portfolio
works.summary: A plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript portfolio with a searchable work library and five mascot themes.
works.description:
This site: a plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript portfolio with a searchable work library and five mascot themes. I built it by hand because I wanted a portfolio I could keep maintaining without a build step or a framework I would have to relearn every semester.

The decision that holds it together is that the content lives in structured JSON and the interface renders it, so the same data drives the site and its editing interface, and a repository snapshot keeps the pages readable whenever the published copy is unavailable.
works.role: Solo developer — site architecture, theme system, and the editing workspace.

works.title: XFCE Desktop Dotfiles
works.summary: An earlier documented XFCE desktop setup using the Tokyo Night color scheme, Xfwm, Plank, Alacritty, Thunar, and Bash.
works.description: An earlier documented XFCE desktop setup using the Tokyo Night color scheme, Xfwm, Plank, Alacritty, Thunar, and Bash. It is archived now, and it marks where the desktop customisation habit that later shaped the Klightten interface started.
works.role: Personal desktop configuration, documented and published.

works.title: PTCMed Database
works.summary: A clinical management database covering doctors, patients, billing, relationships, sample records, and integration concepts for structured healthcare data.
works.description: A clinical management database covering doctors, patients, billing, and the relationships between them, with sample records and integration notes for structured healthcare data. It was academic coursework, and the design work sits in the schema: normalised tables, defined relationships, and the joins and aggregates needed to answer real questions about patients and billing.
works.role: Academic project — relational schema, SQL queries, and sample records.
